narrative:
The 2026 Boston Red Sox opened the year with promise and peril in equal measure, stumbling out of the gate at 1-4 in March before a shaky April left them below .500 at 11-15. The bullpen was already flashing warning signs, with Greg Weissert surrendering a pair of crushing home runs in back-to-back games late in March, and Aroldis Chapman proving to be a persistent liability throughout the middle months. The early returns were sobering, but the roster had enough talent to believe a turnaround was possible.

May and June steadied the ship without fully righting it — 13-14 and 12-14 records that felt like treading water. But beneath those modest numbers, bright spots were emerging. Willson Contreras delivered a massive two-run blast in mid-May, and Masataka Yoshida chipped in timely hits that kept Boston in contention. Then came July, a month that transformed the season entirely. The Red Sox went a scorching 21-4, the best stretch in recent franchise memory, powered by Wilyer Abreu's towering home run on July 18 and Ceddanne Rafaela's grand slam on July 27. Boston had arrived as a genuine playoff contender.

August brought a return to earth — 17-12, still winning but no longer dominant. The bullpen remained a concern, with Chapman continuing to leak runs and Wyatt Olds suffering a wild-pitch nightmare late in the month. But the offense kept answering back: Nick Sogard's clutch double on August 22 and Jarren Duran's grand slam on August 25 kept Boston afloat. September was a .500 slog at 12-12, but Trevor Story's three-run home run on the 17th was the kind of moment that kept the Wild Card dream alive. At 87-75, Boston scratched its way into the postseason by the thinnest of margins.

The Wild Card round against the Yankees proved to be Boston's final chapter. Payton Tolle and Sonny Gray take the ball in back-to-back games, and while moments of resistance flicker — Willson Contreras connecting on a reviewed home run in Game 2, a timely double play here and there — the Yankees keep finding ways to score, with Ben Rice and Luis García Jr. delivering home runs that put Boston's backs against the wall. The Red Sox fall in the Wild Card round, their season ending just one step inside October.

chapters.title: Rough Beginnings
chapters.description: A shaky start to the season sees the Red Sox stumble through March and April, with the bullpen surrendering crucial home runs on back-to-back nights.

chapters.title: Treading Water
chapters.description: Boston goes a combined 25-28 in May and June, mixing encouraging offensive moments with continued pitching breakdowns.

chapters.title: The July Explosion
chapters.description: An electrifying 21-4 July, fueled by Abreu's power and Rafaela's grand slam, vaults the Red Sox into legitimate Wild Card contention.

chapters.title: Holding On
chapters.description: The Red Sox grind through August and September at a winning but unspectacular pace, relying on clutch hits from Sogard, Duran, and Story to stay in the playoff race.

chapters.title: October's Edge
chapters.description: Boston's Wild Card run against the Yankees features isolated moments of fight but ends in elimination as New York's bats prove too much to contain.
